Expected presence and richness at a common depth

Source: R/drarefy.R
el_drarefy.Rd

Counterparts of vegan::drarefy() and vegan::rarefy(): what a random subsample of depth individuals from each sample is expected to contain. There is no randomness, and the results equal vegan's.

Usage

el_drarefy(
  x,
  depth = NULL,
  check = TRUE,
  sample = "sample",
  taxon = "taxon",
  quant = "quant"
)

el_rarefy(
  x,
  depth = NULL,
  check = TRUE,
  sample = "sample",
  taxon = "taxon",
  quant = "quant"
)

Arguments

x

A data frame or lazy duckplyr table with one row per non-zero sample and taxon, holding whole counts. Rows with quant == 0 are dropped.

depth

A single finite whole number, at least 1. The default, NULL, is the smallest total among the samples with a non-zero count, which takes one small query.

check

If TRUE, run queries that stop on negative, missing, non-finite or non-whole counts, warn about samples below depth and stop if none is left. Use FALSE to stay lazy: small samples are still dropped, silently.

sample, taxon, quant

Names of the columns in x. The result has only these three columns, with the same names.

Value

el_drarefy(): a lazy duckplyr table with the columns sample, taxon and quant, named as in the arguments. el_rarefy(): a numeric vector with one expected richness per sample, named by sample.

Details

  • el_drarefy(): for each non-zero cell, the probability that the taxon is in the subsample, 1 - choose(J - x, depth) / choose(J, depth) with J the sample total. Absent taxa have probability 0 and stay absent, so the result is a lazy long table without zeros.

  • el_rarefy(): the sum of these probabilities over a sample, which is its expected richness at depth. Unlike vegan, it has no se option and takes a single depth.

With no depth, the smallest sample total is used, so no sample is dropped. A sample with a total below depth is dropped from the result, with a warning that names it, and it is an error if no sample is left. vegan instead treats such a sample as if depth were its total. A sample whose total equals depth is kept.

The probability depends only on the sample total and the count, so it is computed once for each distinct pair of the two, in R with lchoose() as vegan does. Only these pairs, not the table, are read into R.

Examples

library(dplyr)

# A long table of read counts for 16S ASVs in a time series from the Baltic Sea.
counts <- duckplyr::read_csv_duckdb(
  system.file("extdata", "lmo_free_living.tsv.gz", package = "ecolongr"),
  options = list(delim = "\t", header = TRUE), prudence = "stingy"
)
metadata <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "lmo_free_living_samples.tsv", package = "ecolongr"))

# Samples with at least 5,000 reads.
deep <- counts |>
  summarise(reads = sum(quant, na.rm = TRUE), .by = sample) |>
  filter(reads >= 5000) |>
  select(sample)
counts <- semi_join(counts, deep, by = "sample")
metadata <- filter(metadata, sample %in% as.data.frame(deep)$sample)
# Expected richness of each sample in a subsample of 5,000 reads.
expected <- el_rarefy(counts, depth = 5000)
observed <- el_specnumber(counts)
head(cbind(observed, expected = expected[names(observed)]))
#>                               observed expected
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017      406 255.0769
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1018      361 235.8478
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1019      354 234.3010
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1020      433 304.5102
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1021      313 226.4471
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1022      444 296.1962

# The probability that each ASV is in such a subsample, as a lazy table.
counts |>
  el_drarefy(depth = 5000) |>
  head() |>
  as.data.frame()
#>                          sample                            taxon     quant
#> 1 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 b3cbeae7d7560b285766ebf0563e38cf 0.9996520
#> 2 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 d07fb2a7fa23f10839ea64b47e4dde84 0.2195486
#> 3 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 a47939feccc5b2427f5aaed5e10f9d4e 0.5127092
#> 4 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 e795c18a7a9d8a44c319d3141bad3bbe 0.5695189
#> 5 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 b5ef80188c610dbd0b5f6a3c3595c61a 0.9999997
#> 6 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 63003fc2bf33e0a1679d94ddd16c690d 0.9611575
